title: If a foreigner's drug case ends with a fine, is their stay in Korea safe?
summary: Foreigners go through immigration procedures separately from the criminal process. This article sets out the standards for deportation depending on the type of sentence, and the issues that remain when a case ends with a fine or a suspended indictment.

body.text: When a foreigner who works or has a family in Korea becomes involved in a drug case, the first thing the family asks about is usually not the sentence but their stay. They want to know whether they can keep living here if the punishment is light. The answer is not decided by the criminal outcome alone, because the Immigration Act operates separately from the criminal process.
Standards for deportation

The Immigration Act expressly makes a person who has been sentenced to imprisonment without labor (금고) or a heavier sentence and then released subject to deportation (Article 46(1)13). A typical example is someone released after serving a prison sentence. A person in whom a ground for entry ban arises or is discovered after entry is also subject to deportation (item 3 of the same paragraph), and the grounds for entry ban include drug addicts and persons who are feared to harm social order or good morals (Article 11(1)).

So even if a case ends with a fine or a suspended indictment (기소유예), there is still a chance of becoming subject to immigration review. A fine is not ‘imprisonment without labor or a heavier sentence’, but the fact that the case involves drugs may be assessed in connection with the grounds for entry ban, and it may also count against you in reviews for extension of stay or change of status.

For this reason, in cases involving foreigners, we factor in the effect on immigration procedures when setting the goal for the criminal outcome. Even with the same suspended sentence, what happens next can differ depending on the type of status of stay and the person's life in Korea.
Procedures that begin as the criminal process ends

Public officials who discover a person subject to deportation in the course of their duties must notify the immigration office, and correctional facilities must also report foreigners whose release has been decided (Article 84). So immigration review often begins around the time the criminal process is wrapping up.

If the review finds the person subject to deportation, a deportation order is issued, and the person may file an objection with the Minister of Justice within 7 days of receiving the order (Articles 59 and 60(1)). Even a person subject to deportation may be given a departure order if they wish to leave voluntarily at their own expense (Article 68), and a person who left after receiving a deportation order may be banned from entry for 5 years (Article 11(1)6).
Permanent residents and leaving Korea during an investigation

Permanent residents are in principle not deported, but there are exceptions, such as persons released after being sentenced to imprisonment with or without labor for 5 years or more who fall under the Ministry of Justice ordinance (Article 46(2)). If the charge carries a heavy statutory penalty, such as importing or trafficking, the first step is to examine whether this exception could apply.

A foreigner under investigation or on trial may be barred from leaving Korea (Article 29). Because foreigners can leave the country at any time, the risk of flight tends to be rated highly, so at a pre-arrest detention hearing (영장실질심사) you need to show your life in Korea with materials on your residence, job, family and length of stay. If you have a basis for staying, such as marriage migration or employment, it is a good idea to prepare to explain those circumstances both in the criminal process and in the immigration review.

If your Korean is limited, you can request an interpreter during questioning. You should sign only after checking that what was interpreted has been recorded accurately in the record of statements, because a record you signed without understanding it is hard to correct later.

author: kim-hansol

title: Complainant interviews: victims need to prepare too
summary: It is easy to think that once you file a complaint, the police will work everything out. This article covers where a victim's statement tends to waver in a complainant interview and what to prepare in advance.

body.text: People questioned as suspects get nervous and prepare, but complainants usually don't. Since they are the ones who were harmed, they assume they only need to say what happened. Yet quite a few people come out of a complainant interview saying they couldn't say things the way they meant to. The tension of the interview room affects complainants just as much.
What you are asked in a complainant interview

The investigator goes back over the complaint point by point. They check dates and amounts and who said what, and if the accused has already been questioned, they may tell you the other side's rebuttal and ask what you think. If you give numbers that differ from your complaint, or you are thrown by the other side's claims and start rambling, the credibility of your statement suffers. A face-to-face confrontation interview (대질 조사) with the other party may also be scheduled; if that would be very difficult for you, tell the investigator in advance.

In complaint cases, the complainant's statement often becomes the key evidence. That is why whether your statement stays consistent from start to finish directly affects the outcome. When you are interviewed several weeks after filing the complaint, you may not remember exactly what you wrote.

The investigator may also ask about facts that were not in the complaint. Rather than stating the first memory that comes to mind as if you were certain, it is safer to say ‘I will check and submit materials.’ If a guess you make on the spot later conflicts with the materials, this time it is the complainant's statement that loses credibility.
What to do before the interview

items: Reread the complaint you filed and check the dates and amounts
Write down the rebuttals the other side is likely to make and prepare answers and materials for them
Bring the original evidence (mobile phone, contracts, medical certificates)
Be prepared to say you don't know when you don't remember

body.text: If some of the other side's rebuttals are true, it is better not to hide them. A statement that admits unfavorable facts first and then explains why it is still a crime holds up to the end. If a fact you hid comes out through the other side's materials, the whole complaint starts to be doubted. Interviews can run long, so keep your schedule open that day, and bring your ID, a copy of the complaint and a list of evidence.
You don't have to go alone

When a related party such as a complainant is interviewed, they can have counsel present and assisting in the same way as in the questioning of a suspect (Article 13(3) of the Investigation Rules (수사준칙)). Counsel can sit next to you, give advice and take notes. Jisan goes with clients to complainant interviews, helps with their statements and checks the direction of the investigation revealed during the interview.

If, after the interview, there are facts you left out or new materials you have found, we put them together in a written opinion and submit it. It needs to go in before the police reach a conclusion to be taken into account. The approach to reading and signing the record of statements is no different from that for suspects.

Ask for corrections wherever something is written differently from what you said. A complaint does not end on the day you file it. Until the case reaches a conclusion, the complainant remains a party to that case.

author: kim-hansol

title: Counsel in the interview room does not answer for you
summary: Many people expect that if counsel is present, they will block difficult questions on their behalf. This article explains what counsel actually does in the interview room and what they cannot do.

body.text: There is a question we often hear the day before questioning from people who have decided to be questioned with counsel present: ‘If a difficult question comes up, you'll answer it for me, right?’ Contrary to that expectation, the person who answers questions in the interview room is the suspect. If counsel speaks in your place, it cannot count as the suspect's statement.
Counsel's role as set by law

When a suspect or their family requests it, the judicial police officer must allow counsel to take part in the questioning unless there is a justifiable reason not to (Article 243-2(1) of the Criminal Procedure Act). Counsel who takes part may state an opinion after the questioning ends, may object to improper methods of questioning even during the questioning, and may state an opinion with the investigator's approval (paragraph 3 of the same article).

The Investigation Rules (수사준칙) provide that counsel should sit where they can give real assistance, such as next to the suspect, and that legal advice, consultation and note-taking for that purpose must be allowed (Article 13(1) of the Investigation Rules). Counsel's participation cannot be refused on the grounds that it is merely an interview rather than questioning (paragraph 2 of the same article).

Opinions stated by counsel are written into the record of statements, and counsel also reads and signs that record (paragraph 4 of the same article). Matters regarding counsel's participation or any restriction on it are also recorded. The fact that what happened in the interview room is left on record means more than you might think.
What counsel actually does in the room

items: Points out the way a question is asked when it assumes a conclusion rather than a fact (‘Why did you deceive them?’)
Notes that a question has already been answered when the same question is repeated in different words
Requests a break when the suspect seems exhausted
Reminds the suspect not to guess when their memory is unclear
Reads the record together with the suspect to find places where the wording has changed

body.text: Counsel does not whisper answers to you. Instead, they can notice the moment you stray from the direction agreed in advance and stop it. That is why the value of having counsel present depends greatly on how much you prepared together before the questioning.
If you want to consult counsel during questioning, just say so. Asking for a moment to consult is a suspect's legitimate right, and there is no reason for the request itself to be held against you.
Being present without preparation is only half the job

Counsel meeting you for the first time on the day of questioning will find it hard to know which parts of the case are risky. Only by drawing up expected questions, practicing answers in advance, and deciding how far to speak and which questions to decline to answer can counsel see where to step in during the questioning. That is why Jisan holds practice sessions before questioning. In practice, we ask the questions an investigator is likely to ask, in the way they would actually ask them, and find together where your answers waver.

Counsel in the interview room is less someone who fights on your behalf and more someone who watches over the proceedings with you and makes sure they are on record. Simply having someone watching beside you can change the tone of the questions.

author: kim-hansol

title: Is it fraud if someone can't repay? The test lies in the day the money was borrowed
summary: Not every failure to get lent money back is fraud. This article explains how investigators look at the circumstances on the day the money changed hands.

body.text: “The person who borrowed money from me has cut off contact. If I file a fraud complaint, will I get it back?” This is one of the questions we hear most often on consultation calls. From the other side, we hear people complain that they are being treated as fraudsters when they were only late because their business was struggling. This happens because the two sides are looking at different points in time in the same case.
The clock for fraud stops on the day the money was received

Fraud requires an act of deception, the other person being deceived into handing over money, and a resulting gain. So rather than the later outcome of non-payment, what matters is whether, on the day the money was received, there was an intention and ability to repay. If circumstances worsened after the money was received and it could not be repaid, it is in principle a civil matter.

Investigators compare the borrower's income and assets at that time, how much other debt they had, what they said the money was for, and where it was actually spent. If they said it was for hospital bills but spent it on something else, or if they hid that their debts had already piled up to the point where repayment was difficult, the case leans toward fraud.

Conversely, if the borrower explained the business and its risks as they were when receiving the money, and actually put the money into that business, it is hard to say they deceived anyone even if the outcome was bad. This is why, in investment cases, the business plan and the record of how the funds were used are laid side by side and compared.
What a record of partial repayment tells

Repaying part of the money does not rule out fraud, because the test is the point at which the money was received. However, a record of steadily sending interest and explaining the situation is circumstantial evidence that there was no intention to deceive from the start, and it is also taken into account as restitution.

If you are the one accused, the first step is not to rely on memory but to gather bank transaction records, messages exchanged at the time and business-related contracts in date order. Dated materials carry far more weight than verbal explanations.
News of a higher statutory penalty: it depends on when the conduct took place

With the amendment to the Criminal Act on December 23, 2025, the statutory penalty for fraud became imprisonment for up to 20 years or a fine of up to 50 million won. However, the Criminal Act in principle punishes conduct under the law in force at the time of the act (Article 1 of the Criminal Act), so the previous statutory penalty applies to cases where the money was received before then. Here too, the date the money changed hands is the standard.

If the amount gained is 500 million won or more, the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes (특정경제범죄법) applies and there is no longer a path to ending with a fine. Since the amount can differ depending on whether money received in several installments is treated as one or separately, it is necessary to calculate it transaction by transaction.
A complaint does not collect the money for you

There is something victims should know. Criminal proceedings exist for punishment, so filing a complaint alone does not get your money back. If the other party still has assets, you need to consider provisional attachment (가압류) and a claim for damages together to have a chance of recovering it. Sometimes the other party repays during the investigation to reach a settlement, but that is entirely up to them.

In cases where it is unclear whether it is fraud or a civil matter, rushing to file a complaint can end in a finding of no charges (혐의없음) with only time lost. It is better to decide which path is right after first laying out the materials from the day the money changed hands.

author: kim-hansol

title: Assault ends with a settlement, so why is bodily injury different?
summary: Even in the same fight, if the case is treated as assault, a statement of non-desire for punishment ends it, but if it becomes bodily injury, you can be punished even after settling. This article looks at what a medical certificate means and when to settle.

body.text: A quarrel over drinks that ends with some shoving and a punch or two. In consultations like this, the first thing we ask is whether the other person submitted a medical certificate. That single piece of paper often decides which path the case will take.
Assault and bodily injury: settlement has different effects

Simple assault is punishable by imprisonment for up to 2 years, a fine of up to 5 million won, detention or a petty fine, and if the victim states that they do not want the offender punished, an indictment cannot be filed (Article 260 of the Criminal Act). Intimidation has the same structure. This means that if a settlement is reached, there is no punishment at all.

Bodily injury carries a heavier statutory penalty of imprisonment for up to 7 years, suspension of qualifications for up to 10 years or a fine of up to 10 million won, and it can be punished even if the victim does not want punishment (Article 257 of the Criminal Act). A settlement weighs heavily in the disposition and sentence, but it does not end the case.
A medical certificate does not automatically make it bodily injury

Assault is the use of physical force against a person's body, so pushing someone or throwing an object can also count. Bodily injury goes further and requires a result in which the person's health has deteriorated. If the wound is minor enough to heal on its own, bodily injury is sometimes not recognized even with a medical certificate.

So we check how many days after the incident the certificate was issued, whether the diagnosis matches what happened, and whether there are records of actual treatment. If the charge is settled as assault, the weight of the case changes completely.
If you were hit first, is it self-defense?

An act to protect oneself or another from a present and unjust infringement is not punished if there is a reasonable ground (Article 21 of the Criminal Act). However, if both sides fought with the intention of attacking each other, it is difficult to have self-defense recognized merely because you were hit first. The court looks at whether it was an act of defense, whether it went beyond what was needed to block the attack, and whether there was another way to avoid it.

So we break down the sequence captured on CCTV scene by scene and set out who laid hands first and how many blows were exchanged. There is also a provision that even an act that went too far may not be punished if it was due to fear or panic at night or in another unsettling situation (paragraph 3 of the same article).
A statement of non-desire for punishment has a deadline and required wording

A statement that the victim does not want the offender punished can be made until the first-instance judgment is pronounced, and once made, it cannot be reversed by saying they want punishment after all (Article 232 of the Criminal Procedure Act). Over time, the victim may change their mind, so there is little reason to delay a settlement.

If only settlement money changes hands and the wording on non-desire for punishment is left out, even a simple assault case goes ahead. You should check that the settlement agreement includes a sentence stating that the victim does not want punishment, and that the document has actually been submitted to the investigating authority or the court.

If the other side demands an unreasonable amount, remember that you are not obliged to settle. You can propose a reasonable range based on the extent of the injury and the medical costs, and if no settlement is reached in the end, you can show your intention to compensate the victim through a criminal deposit (형사공탁). If punches were exchanged on both sides, you should also document your own injuries and the circumstances of your defense so you can respond if the case leans toward mutual assault.

author: kim-hansol

title: Repeat drunk driving: where does the ‘10 years’ start?
summary: The statutory penalty for drunk driving is set by blood alcohol concentration and any record within 10 years. This article explains how the 10 years are counted and the figures for license sanctions, which proceed separately from criminal punishment.

body.text: When someone caught drunk driving comes in for a consultation, after their blood alcohol reading there is one more thing we always ask: whether they have ever been punished for drunk driving before, and if so, when that sentence became final. For a second offense, that single date changes which provision applies.
For a first offense, the reading sets the statutory penalty

items: 0.03 percent or more but less than 0.08 percent: imprisonment for up to 1 year or a fine of up to 5 million won
0.08 percent or more but less than 0.2 percent: imprisonment for 1 to 2 years or a fine of 5 million to 10 million won
0.2 percent or more: imprisonment for 2 to 5 years or a fine of 10 million to 20 million won

body.text: These ranges are all set out in Article 148-2(3) of the Road Traffic Act. What is punished is the reading at the time of driving, so depending on the gaps between the time of the last drink, the time of driving and the time of measurement, there may be room to dispute the reading at the time of driving. However, the mere possibility that the level was still rising does not decide the matter.
The 10 years are counted from the date the sentence became final

If you drive drunk again within 10 years of the date a sentence of a fine or heavier for drunk driving or refusing a breath test became final, the aggravated provision applies. Even for a reading of 0.03 percent or more but less than 0.2 percent, a minimum penalty applies: imprisonment for 1 to 5 years or a fine of 5 million to 20 million won (Article 148-2(1)). The standard is not the date you were caught but the date the sentence in the earlier case became final, and that sentence counts toward the 10 years even if it has lapsed.

If you find your earlier judgment or summary order (약식명령) and confirm the exact date it became final, you can immediately see which provision will apply. You should also be aware that even if 10 years have passed, it is still considered a prior conviction for the same type of offense in sentencing.
Your license is handled separately from criminal punishment

Suspension and revocation of a driver's license are administrative sanctions by the provincial police agency commissioner, so they proceed separately from the criminal process. Under Appended Table 28 of the Enforcement Rules of the Road Traffic Act, a reading of 0.03 percent or more but less than 0.08 percent carries 100 penalty points and a license suspension, with the suspension period in principle counted as one day per penalty point. A reading of 0.08 percent or more, injuring someone while under the influence, or refusing a breath test leads to revocation. For someone with a prior drunk driving record, a reading of just 0.03 percent or more means revocation.

If driving is your livelihood, you can file an objection seeking a reduction within 60 days of the date of the sanction. However, you are not eligible for a reduction if your blood alcohol concentration exceeded 0.1 percent, you injured someone, you refused a breath test, or you have a drunk driving record within 5 years. A person whose license was revoked for a repeat violation within 5 years must obtain a conditional license with an alcohol ignition interlock device installed to drive again (Article 80-2 of the Road Traffic Act).
Sentencing materials must be verifiable

Rather than a single letter of apology, what is taken into account is material that can actually be verified, such as having sold your car or stopped driving, or records of alcohol counseling or treatment. If the fine in a summary order feels too heavy, you can request a formal trial within 7 days of being notified, but the fine may also go up, so you should weigh this carefully before making the request.

author: kim-hansol

title: Sex crime questioning: the last 10 minutes before you sign the record
summary: After hours of questioning, anyone wants to leave quickly. But the time spent reading the record of statements is your last chance to correct your statement.

body.text: When questioning ends, the investigator hands you the printed record of statements and tells you to read it and sign if there is nothing wrong. You have already been sitting for hours and your mind is tired. Even without the investigator rushing you, you rush yourself, and many people flip through only the first few pages and sign the last one.

This moment is a pity because the record follows you through every later stage. The same record sits at the front of the file for the police's decision on whether to refer the case, the disposition by the prosecutor at the Public Prosecution Office (공소청), and the trial. If you say something different in court, you first have to explain why your statement changed.
The right to read and the right to correct

The record must be shown or read aloud to the suspect, and if the suspect asks for a correction, it must be added to the record. The original part objected to is left so that it can still be read (Article 244(2) of the Criminal Procedure Act). Making corrections is not a favor; it is a procedure set by law.

If you don't have enough time, ask for more. If you request it in writing, reading the record is recognized as an exception to the 12-hour limit on total questioning time, and even under the restriction on late-night questioning, the reading can continue until midnight (Articles 21(1) and 22(1) of the Investigation Rules (수사준칙)). If counsel is present, you can read it together and check the wording one phrase at a time. If counsel stated an opinion after the questioning, the record containing that opinion is also shown to counsel for signature (Article 243-2(4) of the Criminal Procedure Act).
Where to look in those 10 minutes

items: Sentences containing words you did not use
Places where the question is long and your answer is recorded only as ‘yes’
Numbers such as times, frequencies and places
Whether things you said you didn't remember have turned into definite statements
Your answer to the final question of whether you have anything to add

body.text: In sex crime records, the verbs describing the act are especially important. Brushed against, touched, felt, grabbed: the same contact can be assessed differently in law depending on the word. Just checking that the record uses the words you actually used makes these 10 minutes worthwhile.

Also look closely at any part where the victim's statement was summarized to you and you were asked what you thought. If you answered that it might be possible, check that your answer has not been written up as if you accepted the victim's statement.

At the end of the record, you write by hand that you have no objections or comments, stamp across the pages and sign (Article 244(3) of the Criminal Procedure Act). If you asked for a correction and it was not made, ask that the fact that you made the request be recorded.
What you can still do after signing

You cannot undo a record you have already signed. However, if you write down which questions you were asked and how you answered right after the questioning, while your memory is fresh, any misunderstandings can be pointed out and explained in a written opinion from counsel. If further questioning or a confrontation is scheduled, the wording of the first record becomes the starting point for the next questions, so it is essential to take time to go over things again before then.

author: kim-hansol

title: When you hear nothing after questioning: what to do in the meantime
summary: When weeks go by after questioning with no word, anxiety grows. This article explains why the waiting period is not empty time.

body.text: A few weeks after questioning, the calls come: ‘I haven't heard anything. What's going on?’ When you ask the police station, the only answer is that it is under review. You can't tell whether no news is good news or something bigger is being prepared, so every day feels long.
There is now a deadline for a decision, but

From October 2, 2026, the police must finish investigating cases initiated by a complaint or accusation and decide whether to refer them within 3 months of accepting them (Article 238 of the Criminal Procedure Act). However, this deadline applies to complaint and accusation cases, not to cases the police discovered and started on their own. Cases with many people involved or that require analysis of materials may take longer to reach an actual conclusion.

There is no need to assume that a long wait is a bad sign. There is just one thing to remember: until the result comes out, the decision has not been made, and materials submitted in the meantime are also considered.

If you want to know how things are going, asking the investigator about once a month or checking through counsel is enough. The investigator may contact you to request additional materials or schedule further questioning; if so, asking what they want to confirm will make it easier to prepare.
Organizing what you couldn't say in the interview room

On the way home from questioning, there is always something you wish you had said. You may have given a wrong number in a moment of panic, or had materials at home that would have explained things but didn't bring them. Before your memory fades, write down the questions you were asked and your answers. Mark separately any questions you couldn't answer or answered vaguely.

You can apply to inspect and copy the record containing your own statement (Article 69(1) of the Investigation Rules (수사준칙)). After checking how the record was written, if you put the missing explanations and materials together in a written opinion and submit it, it will be reviewed together when deciding whether to refer the case. A written opinion is only meaningful if it goes in before the decision is made. One submitted after the conclusion has been reached becomes a request to overturn a decision already made.
What not to do while waiting

items: Calling the investigator in charge every few days to press for a result
Contacting the complainant directly and asking them to withdraw the complaint
Writing a different account from the one you gave during questioning in a written opinion without materials to back it up

body.text: Be especially careful about contacting the complainant directly. Even if you meant to apologize, the other side can easily feel pressured, and that contact goes back into the investigation file. If a settlement is needed, it is better to find out the other side's wishes through counsel first.

If you admit the allegations, this period is also a good time to prepare for a settlement. If restitution is made before the decision on referral, it can be reflected both in the police's decision and in the prosecutor's decision afterward.

The result is usually notified by text message (Article 53 of the Investigation Rules). If you receive a text about referral or non-referral, don't delete it; keep it along with the case number. The next step starts from that message.

author: kim-hansol

title: Division of property after divorce: a 2-year period that cannot be extended
summary: The right to claim division of property expires 2 years after the date of divorce, and this period cannot be interrupted or extended. This article looks at what an exclusion period means, the risk of claiming only part of the property, and the effect of a written waiver.

body.text: In legal consultations, people often talk about the ‘statute of limitations’: that sending a certified letter stops the clock, or that it starts again if the other side says they will pay. None of this applies to the 2 years for division of property after divorce.
It is an exclusion period, not a statute of limitations

Article 839-2(3) of the Civil Act provides that the right to claim division of property expires when 2 years have passed from the date of divorce. These 2 years are an exclusion period (제척기간), so they do not stop or get extended because you made a demand to the other side. The right is preserved only if you file a petition for mediation or a request for adjudication with the family court within the period. The same provision applies to judicial divorce (Article 843).

The ‘date of divorce’ that serves as the standard is the date the divorce was registered for a divorce by agreement, and the date the judgment became final for a judicial divorce. You can confirm the exact date by obtaining a detailed marriage relationship certificate. Remember that the period keeps running even while the other side drags things out, saying they will sort it out soon.

People who put off talking about property at the time of a divorce by agreement need to be especially careful. Right after the divorce, emotions are still raw and you avoid contact, and only after about a year, once life has settled, does the property issue come to mind. If the other side then says ‘just wait a little longer’, several more months go by. Even if you keep talking, calculate the expiry date separately and be ready to file before then.
If you claimed only part of the property

In its decision 2018Seu18 of June 22, 2018, the Supreme Court held that if only part of the property was claimed for division within 2 years, the right to claim the remaining property expires when the period passes. Filing a lawsuit within 2 years does not protect all the property; only the property claimed is protected.

The same decision said that if property that was not addressed at all in the proceedings is newly discovered after the decision becomes final, an additional claim can be made, but that additional claim must also be made within 2 years of the date of divorce. So it is safer to list all the property you know about when you first file, and to state that you will expand the claim based on the results of the property inquiry for any property still being confirmed.
If you signed a waiver

Signing a statement such as ‘I will not make any claim regarding property in the future’ does not block a claim in every case. Its effect may be judged differently depending on whether it was a statement vaguely waiving rights before the divorce took effect, or an agreement reached after reviewing all the property and completing a settlement. Setting out the date you signed, the property you knew about at the time and how you came to sign can be used to challenge its effect.
If property disappeared in the meantime

If the other side transferred property to someone else to avoid division, you can file a claim to revoke a fraudulent act (사해행위취소) (Article 839-3 of the Civil Act). This lawsuit must be filed within 1 year of learning of the grounds for revocation and within 5 years of the disposal, so you need to keep track of a deadline separate from the 2 years for division of property. If the property has not yet been disposed of, the first step is to apply for provisional attachment or a provisional injunction against disposal along with the claim.

If there is not much time left, the right order is to file first, even if you haven't gathered all the materials, and supplement through a property inquiry. If you learn of hidden property after the 2 years have passed, it is not easy to find another way.

author: kim-miso

title: Nullity and annulment of marriage: how are they different from divorce?
summary: If there was never an intention to become spouses, you seek nullity of marriage; if you married because you were deceived or coerced, you seek annulment. This article compares the requirements and deadlines of the three paths and the consequences for children and records.

body.text: “I don't want a divorce on my record. Can't the marriage itself be treated as if it never happened?” This is a question often asked by people who have been through a fraudulent marriage or a marriage for the purpose of entering Korea. Besides divorce, the law provides two other paths, nullity and annulment of marriage, but the requirements are strict and the deadlines short, so you first need to decide which path to take.
Nullity of marriage: when there was no agreement from the start

Article 815(1) of the Civil Act provides that a marriage is null if there is no agreement to marry between the parties. In its judgment 2010Meu574 of June 10, 2010, the Supreme Court viewed an agreement to marry as a meeting of minds to form the mental and physical union that society recognizes as a married couple. If one side was sincere but the other registered the marriage as a means to enter Korea or get a job, the marriage is null even if they agreed to the registration itself.

If the other side secretly forged documents and registered the marriage, you can also claim nullity because there was no agreement to marry. Nullity of marriage can be claimed without any time limit (Article 23 of the Family Litigation Act), and it goes straight to a lawsuit without mediation. Once nullity becomes final, the marriage is treated as never having existed, and the family relationship register is corrected according to the judgment. On the other hand, the relationship going sour after the wedding is a matter for divorce, not nullity.
Annulment of marriage: a path with short deadlines

Annulment is sought when, for example, a person married due to fraud or duress, or did not know at the time of marriage of a serious illness or other grave reason that makes married life impossible to continue (Article 816 of the Civil Act). For fraud or duress, a claim cannot be made once 3 months have passed from the date the fraud was discovered or the duress ended (Article 823), and for a grave reason, once 6 months have passed from the date the reason became known (Article 822).

Fraud does not mean there is a duty to disclose everything in the past. The question is what was hidden and how important it was to the decision to marry. Even commonly disputed matters such as hidden debts or education do not lead to annulment by themselves; the court also looks at whether there was active deception and how it affected the decision.

Duress is when threats or violence led to a marriage the person did not want. In this case, the period is counted from the date the person escaped the duress. If they were threatened continuously while living together, when that situation ended becomes the issue, so materials such as the date they left home and records of police reports become important.
The consequences differ as follows

items: Nullity of marriage: the marriage is treated as never having existed, and children born in the meantime become children born out of wedlock (Article 855(1) of the Civil Act)
Annulment of marriage: the effect does not go back in time; the marriage ends when the judgment becomes final (Article 824)
In an annulment, custody of children and visitation follow the same provisions as divorce (Article 824-2)
Damages for emotional distress can be claimed from the party responsible for the nullity or annulment (Articles 825 and 806)

body.text: If the deadline for annulment has passed or nullity is hard to prove, we change direction and consider divorce and consolation money (위자료). ‘When did you find out’ is often what is disputed, so whichever path you take, the starting point is to immediately keep messages or records from the day you learned the facts.

author: kim-miso

title: Divorce by agreement: what the judge doesn't ask
summary: At the confirmation hearing for a divorce by agreement, the court checks only the intention to divorce and matters concerning the children. Unless division of property and consolation money are settled separately, they remain blank even after the divorce.

body.text: The time you stand before the judge at the confirmation hearing for a divorce by agreement is shorter than you might expect. The judge usually asks whether you intend to divorce and, if you have minor children, checks how you have decided on the person with parental authority and child support, and that is it. After going through that brief procedure, it is easy to feel as if the court has settled everything about the divorce.
What the court looks at

Under Articles 836-2 and 837 of the Civil Act, what the court checks is the intention to divorce and the agreement on the person with parental authority and the custodial parent, child support and visitation. The court records child support in a child support obligation protocol (양육비부담조서), which, like a judgment, serves as a basis for compulsory execution. In effect, the parts that go through confirmation also come with a way to collect later.

That does not mean the court looks at the agreement on the children only as a formality. If the terms do not serve the child's welfare, the court orders corrections, and if they are not corrected, it will not confirm the intention to divorce. If you write only the amount of child support and leave the payment date or end date blank, disputes arise as soon as overdue amounts need to be calculated, so make clear at the agreement stage which day of the month, to which account and until when payments will be made.
Property and consolation money remain blank

Division of property and consolation money (위자료) are not subject to confirmation. The judge does not ask about them, and unless the two of you agree separately, they remain unsettled even after the divorce is registered.

That does not mean the rights disappear. A person divorced by agreement can also claim division of property (Article 839-2 of the Civil Act), as long as they do so within 2 years of the date of divorce. The problem is when the other side disposes of property or cuts off contact in the meantime. Property that was visible while you lived in the same home can only be seen through court proceedings after the divorce.
Blanks often found in agreements
Even if you write an agreement, if the wording is brief, you end up disputing its interpretation again. These are the things often missing from agreements we see in consultations.

items: Consolation money and division of property are not separated and are written as a single amount
There is a payment deadline but no late-payment damages if payment is delayed
The house is to be transferred, but there is no date for handing over the registration documents
Who will repay the mortgage loan is left out
There is no mention at all of severance pay and pensions

body.text: If there is money to be received in the future, one option is to have it made into a notarial deed consenting to compulsory execution. However, what can be enforced directly by a notarial deed is limited to things like promises to pay money, so for a transfer of real estate you need to set a separate date for handing over the registration documents.

One more thing to know is that a property division agreement written on the premise of a divorce by agreement may have its effect called into question if the divorce by agreement does not actually take place. If the agreement breaks down and the matter moves to a judicial divorce, division of property may have to be disputed all over again. Rather than thinking everything is over once you have signed the agreement, it is more accurate to think that the agreement only does its job once the divorce has been registered.

A proposal to ‘get divorced first and sort out the rest slowly’ is not wrong in itself. The question is whether you agree knowing what will be left over if you do so. Just checking the list of property against a draft agreement once before the confirmation hearing can save you a lawsuit after the divorce.

author: kim-miso

title: What is often missing from an inheritance division agreement
summary: An agreement is valid only if all heirs take part, and once it takes effect it is hard to undo. This article looks at parts often overlooked in agreements, such as minor heirs, property discovered later and the deceased's debts.

body.text: It is easy to think that once the siblings have talked it through, all that is left is the paperwork. But division of inherited property is a legal act whose effect goes back to the time the inheritance began (Article 1015 of the Civil Act), so a single phrase in the agreement can determine registration, banking matters and even later disputes.
First, did everyone take part?

Division by agreement requires the participation of all co-heirs. They don't need to gather in one place; the agreement can be passed around for each to sign and affix their registered seal. But if even one person is left out, the agreement has no effect. More often than you might think, people are left out, such as children from a marriage before remarriage, or heirs by representation (대습상속인) like the spouse and children of a sibling who died earlier.

If a mother and her minor children are heirs together, the mother cannot represent the children in the agreement. Because their interests conflict, a special representative must be appointed by the family court for each child (Article 921 of the Civil Act). If there are two children, each has a separate special representative.

A person whose renunciation of inheritance has been accepted was never an heir from the start, so they are left out of the agreement, and the court decision on the renunciation is attached at registration. Conversely, an heir who has lost contact and whose whereabouts are unknown cannot simply be left out, so you apply to the family court for appointment of an administrator of an absentee's property, and the administrator takes part in the agreement with the court's permission.
Describe property exactly as in the register and bankbook

For real estate, you need to write the lot number and area, and for deposits, the bank and account number, so that the agreement can be used as is for registration and closing accounts. It is also a good idea to include a clause on what to do with property discovered later. Without it, a single newly found bankbook means getting everyone's seal again.
Agreeing to take nothing is not the same as renouncing the inheritance

Some people think that because they agreed to take nothing in the agreement, they have no debts either. But that only settles how the family divides the property; it is not a renunciation of inheritance that releases you from debts to creditors. To avoid inheriting debts, you must file a renunciation or qualified acceptance (한정승인) with the family court within 3 months, and if you do things in the wrong order, stamping your seal on the agreement could be seen as disposing of inherited property.
Debts are not settled by the agreement alone

Siblings can agree among themselves that the person who receives the house will repay all of the deceased's loans. However, the deceased's monetary debts pass to each heir according to their share of inheritance, so unless the bank consents to that assumption of debt, the other siblings remain liable to the bank (Article 454 of the Civil Act). The same goes for the obligation to return a tenant's deposit, so write down who will bear it and notify the bank and the tenant.

Notarization is not a requirement for validity, but once an agreement takes effect, it is hard to undo on the grounds of a change of heart. Before stamping your seal, please calculate at least once what your share is after reflecting special benefits (특별수익) and contributions (기여분). If this overlaps with the inheritance tax filing deadline (6 months from the last day of the month in which the inheritance began), it is also a good idea to get a tax review.

author: kim-miso

title: What happens at a mediation hearing for division of inherited property?
summary: Most adjudications for division of inherited property begin with a mediation hearing. This article explains what goes on in the mediation room and what to prepare.

body.text: When you file for adjudication of division of inherited property, the first notice is usually not for an adjudication hearing but for a mediation hearing. This is because the Family Litigation Act requires these cases to go through mediation first. Many people picture standing before a judge in a courtroom and are taken aback to find themselves sitting across from a mediator in a small room. If you have a picture of it in advance, you can say what you need to say much more calmly on the day.
The scene in the mediation room

Mediation is a procedure in which a judge or mediator listens to both sides and looks for a point where agreement is possible. Since all heirs are parties, siblings often gather in one room, and depending on the atmosphere, the mediator may also hear each side separately. If voices are raised, the mediator puts the discussion back in order.

The mediator does not force a conclusion. Instead, they keep asking whether you could accept this or that. If you have no standard of your own at that point, you either give in to the atmosphere and agree, or end up rejecting every proposal.
Mediation often does not end in one session and continues over several hearings. It is common to recalculate the other side's proposal between hearings and respond at the next one.

When talk turns to your parents, emotions easily take over. Who was the more devoted child, or who caused hurt, may be the biggest issue in your heart, but in the mediation room what matters is how those circumstances translate into numbers. It is better to write down what you want to say in advance and say it briefly.
What you need to bring is numbers

items: A list of the property and market value data for each item
Registry records or remittance records of lifetime gifts received by other heirs
If you are claiming a contribution (기여분), materials showing the period and cost of caring for the deceased
Your own calculation reflecting special benefits and contributions
The minimum you can accept and the reasons for it

body.text: To claim a contribution, you must file a separate request for determination of contribution together with the claim for division. If the court sets and notifies a filing period of at least 1 month, you must file within it, and if the period passes, the request may be dismissed (Article 113 of the Rules on Family Litigation). For a contribution argument to carry weight in mediation, this request needs to be filed first.
If an agreement is reached, and if not

If an agreement is reached, a mediation protocol is drawn up and it has the same effect as a judicial settlement (Article 59(2) of the Family Litigation Act). Registration and settlement payments follow exactly what the protocol says, so before signing, check carefully the description of the property, the payment dates and who bears the taxes. If you can't decide on the spot, you can ask for another hearing date.

If no agreement is reached, the court holds an examination hearing and then calculates each heir's specific share and issues an adjudication. Including mediation, this usually takes about a year, and longer if appraisals or financial inquiries take time. If you cannot attend on a given day, submit a written explanation with the case number and state your views in writing. If you submit no views at all, the matter may be settled mainly on the other siblings' arguments.

author: kim-miso

title: Consolation money in adultery cases: what does the court consider?
summary: There is no set table for consolation money in claims against an affair partner. This article covers the circumstances that come up again and again in the reasons for judgments, and why it is hard to apply the amount in someone else's judgment to your own case.

body.text: The question that comes up most at the start of a consultation is, in the end, how much you can receive or how much you will have to pay. If you search online, you will find many articles stating amounts with certainty. But there is no legally set table for consolation money (위자료) in claims against an affair partner (상간자). Article 751 of the Civil Act only provides that mental suffering must also be compensated; the amount is set by the court by putting together the various circumstances that come out in the proceedings. Because consolation money is not calculated from receipts, assessments of the same circumstances can differ somewhat from one court panel to another.
The amount in the complaint is a starting point

The amount the plaintiff writes in the complaint is the amount the plaintiff wants. It is common for the judgment to set a lower amount, and that does not mean the plaintiff overreached. There is no reason for the defendant to be frightened into thinking they must pay the amount in the complaint. However, keep in mind that if you do not submit a written answer, judgment may be entered for that amount. Stamp fees and service fees vary with the amount claimed, and the costs of the lawsuit may be shared in proportion to the part you lose, so setting the amount as high as possible is not always the answer.
Circumstances that move the amount
If you read the reasons for judgments, there are circumstances the courts mention again and again. No single one sets the amount; the direction is set by several circumstances together.

The nature of the relationship is also considered. Infidelity can be recognized even if sexual relations are not proven, but the court does not treat a case where only romantic messages were exchanged the same as one where the two lived together or traveled together repeatedly.

items: The length of the marriage and whether there are young children
How long the infidelity continued, how often they met and the nature of the relationship
How clearly the affair partner knew that the person was married
Whether the relationship ended after it was discovered, or whether they kept meeting or even mocked the plaintiff
Whether the infidelity led to separation or divorce

body.text: Of these, in practice the attitude after discovery makes a noticeable difference. Records of meetings after being caught, or insulting messages sent to the plaintiff, are grouped together and submitted separately. On the defendant's side, a record showing that contact was cut off on the day of discovery carries the same weight.
Why it is hard to transfer the amount from someone else's judgment

Cases that end in divorce tend to be assessed as causing greater harm than cases where the marriage continues. That does not mean there is no harm when the marriage continues. The suffering of enduring in order to rebuild the relationship is also mental harm. If consolation money has already been received from the spouse, that amount may also be considered in determining the total harm. Psychiatric treatment records are used as material showing that the suffering was great, but the amount is not calculated to increase with the number of visits.

With so many variables, it is hard to plug the amount from someone else's judgment directly into your case. A claim amount is more persuasive when set with supporting materials for each of the circumstances above, and those grounds also become the standard when amounts are exchanged in mediation. The same applies to the defendant. To seek a reduction, rather than simply saying the amount is too high, you need to show with materials which circumstances differ from what the plaintiff claims.

author: kim-miso

title: Can you make a claim against an affair partner if your marriage was never registered?
summary: If a de facto marriage is recognized, you can claim consolation money from the unfaithful spouse and the affair partner. However, you first need to show that it was a de facto marriage and that the affair partner knew of the relationship.

body.text: More couples than you might think have held a wedding ceremony but put off registering their marriage for one reason or another. Then, on discovering a spouse's affair, they hesitate, wondering whether they have no rights because they never registered. The law does not see it that way. If you intended to marry and actually lived as a married couple, you are protected as being in a de facto marriage (사실혼), and you can also hold the affair partner who infringed that relationship responsible.
The starting point is proving it was a de facto marriage

A de facto marriage is recognized only when there is both an intention to marry and the substance of married life together. It is not decided by the length of cohabitation alone; the court looks at whether people around you treated you as a married couple and whether you ran your life together. If it is assessed as cohabitation while dating, it is difficult to claim consolation money from either the partner or the affair partner.

So in de facto marriage cases, materials showing the substance of the relationship are as important as evidence of the infidelity. What a single marriage relationship certificate would settle in a legal marriage has to be filled in with a variety of materials.

items: Wedding photos, wedding invitations, records of the families' formal meeting
Records of attending holidays and family events on both sides together
Account records showing living expenses or loans were shared
Hospital or school documents listing you as spouse or guardian
Move-in records at the same address, lease agreements

body.text: Even if there were periods when you lived apart for work, that does not immediately rule it out. If you held a wedding, attended family events together and lived as a married couple, a de facto marriage may be recognized, so prepare materials showing why you lived apart and how often you saw each other.
The affair partner must have known of the relationship

Because the marriage was not registered, affair partners often argue that they didn't know the two were married. You need materials showing that the affair partner knew the two lived together or had held a wedding. Records of the spouse calling you ‘my wife’ or ‘my husband’ in conversations with the affair partner, records of meetings near the home you shared, and wedding photos posted on social media are used. If the affair partner attended the wedding as a guest, or socialized with the two of you as a couple in the same group, that alone is strong evidence. Conversely, if you did not tell people around you about the marriage, it is that much harder to show what the affair partner knew.
Some de facto marriages are not protected

A de facto marriage with someone who has a legal spouse is, absent special circumstances, not given protection equivalent to a legal marriage. According to case law, the same applies even if the legal spouse had left home long ago (Supreme Court judgment 96Meu530 of September 20, 1996). Conversely, if you are the legal spouse and your spouse is living with someone else as if in a de facto marriage, that person can be held responsible as an affair partner.

A de facto marriage can be ended without any filing, so when an affair comes to light, the end of the relationship, consolation money and property issues are often disputed all at once. A claim for consolation money must be made within 3 years of learning of the harm and the person responsible (Article 766 of the Civil Act), so keep a record of the dates the relationship ended and you learned of the affair. Around this time, you should also decide whether to pursue the claim against your de facto spouse or the claim against the affair partner first, or both together.

author: kim-miso

title: Divorce suit and suit against an affair partner: file together or separately?
summary: If you have decided to divorce, you can bring a case against both your spouse and the affair partner in the family court. This article sets out jurisdiction, mediation and the differences between filing together and separately, focusing on the statutory provisions.

body.text: People considering divorce are often confused, first of all, about when and where to file a lawsuit against the affair partner. A case claiming only against the affair partner while staying married and a case claiming against both the spouse and the affair partner while divorcing are handled by different courts to begin with. Getting the order wrong costs more time and money.
The nature of the case decides the court

A case claiming damages for mental harm from an affair partner's infidelity while staying married is an ordinary civil case, so it is handled by the district court. On the other hand, a claim for damages arising from divorce, including a claim against a third party, is a Category Da (다류) family litigation case under the exclusive jurisdiction of the family court (Article 2(1)1(c)2) of the Family Litigation Act).

Several family litigation cases arising from the same facts can be filed as a single suit, and if they fall under different courts, they can be filed together in a family court that has jurisdiction over one of them (Article 14 of the Family Litigation Act). That is why it is common to name the spouse as Defendant 1 and the affair partner as Defendant 2 in the divorce complaint and claim against both at once.
The family court starts with mediation

Divorce and claims for consolation money arising from divorce in principle go through mediation first. For Category Na (나류) and Da family litigation cases, mediation must be applied for, and even if a suit is filed without applying for mediation, the court in principle refers it to mediation (Article 50 of the Family Litigation Act). If the terms of the divorce and the consolation money from the affair partner are settled together in mediation, the case ends without a trial; if not, it moves on to hearings.
Filing together versus separately

If you file together, the same panel looks at the same evidence at once. Since the spouse's responsibility and the affair partner's responsibility are judged on the same facts, the risk of conflicting conclusions is reduced, and witness examinations and financial record inquiries can be done in one go. If the spouse's card statements show payments for accommodation or gifts, those materials can be used as they are for the claim against the affair partner.

On the other hand, a divorce case also involves division of property and child custody issues, so it tends to take longer. If you want to resolve the affair partner issue first, or have not yet decided whether to divorce, you can also file the suit against the affair partner in the district court first. Conversely, if evidence is lacking, you may consider proceeding with the divorce suit first and strengthening the claim against the affair partner with financial records obtained in that process. Either way, your statements about when and how you learned of the affair must stay the same in both cases.

items: Have you already decided whether to divorce?
Do you want to resolve the affair partner issue quickly, or settle everything at once?
Do you need your spouse's financial records to complete the evidence?
Are there circumstances on your side as plaintiff that could be disputed?

body.text: Why the last question matters

The Supreme Court has held that where both spouses are equally responsible for the breakdown of the marriage and the claim for consolation money against the spouse is dismissed, a third party who took part in the infidelity cannot be held liable for damages arising from the divorce either (Supreme Court judgment 2023Meu16678 of June 27, 2024). When claiming together with a divorce, you should be prepared for the spouse to file a counterclaim alleging fault on your part. Whether to file together or separately should be decided after weighing this risk as well.

author: kim-miso

title: Being recognized as a jeonse fraud victim does not return your deposit for you
summary: Victim recognition opens the door to deferral of auction, a priority purchase right and housing support, but recovering the deposit still happens through civil procedures. This article sets out the requirements and deadlines of the two procedures separately.

body.text: When tenants in the same building all fail to get their deposits back and the building goes to auction, many first think of applying for recognition as a jeonse fraud victim (전세사기피해자 결정). Recognition is certainly an important starting point. But unless you distinguish what it does and does not do for you, you may miss the deadlines in the procedures that actually get you your money.
What recognition opens up

If you are recognized as a victim under the Special Act on Support for Victims of Jeonse Fraud and Housing Stability, you can receive support such as applications for deferral and suspension of auction, a priority purchase right, public rental housing and financial support. On the victim's application, the court may withhold setting a sale date or defer or suspend the auction, for a period of up to 1 year (Article 17). You can also provide security by the sale date and declare that you will buy with priority at the same price as the highest bid (Article 20).
Requirements and who is covered

You must have opposability (대항력) and a fixed-date stamp (확정일자), the deposit must be 500 million won or less (which the committee may raise within a range of 200 million won), damage must have occurred or be expected to occur to multiple tenants, and there must be substantial reason to suspect that the landlord intended not to return the deposits (Article 3). If you can get the full amount back through deposit return insurance, or recover it in full through first-priority repayment (최우선변제) or similar, you are not covered.

The supplementary provisions of the May 20, 2025 amendment apply the Act to tenants who first entered into a lease before May 31, 2025. If you renewed or signed a new lease, first check the date of your original contract. If you first signed after that date, you must recover through ordinary civil procedures.
The money comes through civil procedures

Being recognized as a victim does not mean the state pays your deposit on the landlord's behalf. Recovering the deposit still happens through civil procedures: registration of leasehold (임차권등기), a lawsuit for return of the deposit and distribution from the auction. In an auction, you must file a demand for distribution by the deadline set by the court to receive a distribution, and the amount you can receive is determined by your ranking in the register, your fixed date and any unpaid taxes.

If you object to the victim recognition decision, you must file an objection with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport within 30 days of receiving the decision (Article 15). The recognition procedure and the auction procedure do not wait for each other. Please write the deadlines of both procedures on a single sheet so that you don't miss the deadline for demanding distribution while waiting for the recognition decision, or move your resident registration out before registering your leasehold because you rushed to move.
Who can be held responsible

If the landlord hid from the start that they were unable to return the deposit and signed the contract anyway, you can consider filing a fraud complaint. With the December 23, 2025 amendment, the statutory penalty for fraud became imprisonment for up to 20 years or a fine of up to 50 million won (Article 347 of the Criminal Act). However, a compensation order in a criminal trial is not granted unless the amount of damage is specific, so it is safer to prepare a separate civil claim.

If the licensed real estate agent misexplained the senior rights, you can claim damages, and you may also be able to receive payment from the mutual aid fund or surety insurance the agent has joined. Keep in mind that if there were circumstances you could have checked yourself, the amount may be reduced by comparative negligence.

author: park-jongjin

title: Deductions for restoration costs: what the landlord must prove
summary: Overdue rent and damage caused by the tenant are deducted from the deposit, but the tenant does not bear wear and tear from ordinary use. This article looks at what sets the standard in disputes over deductions.

body.text: On the day you get your deposit back, the settlement statement sometimes comes with a string of unexpected items: the cost of replacing all the wallpaper and flooring, move-in cleaning fees, repairs for nail holes in the walls, and so on. Deducting from the deposit is a legitimate right in itself, but not everything can be deducted.
What can be deducted from the deposit

A deposit is money that secures the tenant's obligations until the lease ends. So overdue rent, unpaid maintenance fees and the cost of repairing damage the tenant caused are deducted from the deposit. However, the landlord who claims a deduction must prove that such a claim arose. If the settlement statement only lists amounts with no basis, you can ask for the basis first.
Restoration does not mean making it new

Restoration to the original state means returning the property to the condition in which the tenant received it, not making it like new. It is generally considered that the tenant has no obligation to fix wear and tear from ordinary use, such as wallpaper faded by sunlight, dents where furniture stood, or faucets worn from long use. On the other hand, doors scratched by pets, walls yellowed by smoking, and marks left from removing fixtures the tenant installed on their own may be the tenant's responsibility.

It is also common for the full replacement cost to be charged when only part is damaged. In that case, the amount can be disputed based on the extent of the damage and how long the material had already been used. A tenant should not have to pay the full price of new flooring because one corner of 10-year-old flooring was dented.

From the landlord's side, giving a settlement statement with the basis for each deduction is the way to reduce disputes. Holding back a large amount without a basis can result in liability for late-payment damages on that portion.
In the end, photos tell the story

items: Dated photos of the walls, floors and fixtures in each room taken on move-in day
Photos and videos taken while checking the condition with the landlord on move-out day
The landlord's estimate and an estimate obtained from another company
Settlement records for maintenance fees and utilities

body.text: Cleaning fees are another frequently disputed item. If the tenant tidied up to a normal standard before leaving, there is little reason for the tenant to pay for professional cleaning for the new tenant. However, if the contract separately provides for a move-out cleaning fee, that agreement must be looked at first.

Without photos from move-in, you have weaker grounds to argue that a flaw was there from the start. If the special terms of the contract set out the scope of restoration, that wording also matters. However, if a special term is written broadly so as to put even ordinary wear and tear on the tenant, there is room to dispute its interpretation.

If you cannot agree to the amount deducted, you can ask for at least the undisputed amount to be returned first. If it still can't be resolved, each item will be decided in a lawsuit for return of the deposit, and for cases where a dispute over deductions is expected, it is better to go to a lawsuit from the start rather than apply for a payment order.

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: Terminating a lease for unpaid rent: two periods for housing, three for commercial premises
summary: A building lease can be terminated when unpaid rent reaches two periods' worth, and a commercial lease covered by the Commercial Building Lease Protection Act when it reaches three periods' worth. This article also covers notice of termination and how the deposit is settled in an eviction suit.

body.text: We are often asked whether a landlord can tell a tenant to leave right away when they have not paid rent for several months. The answer depends on how many payments are overdue, and also on whether it is a home or commercial premises. Rushing to evict without meeting the requirements for termination actually takes longer.
Building leases: two periods

In a building lease, the landlord may terminate the contract when the tenant's unpaid rent reaches the amount of two periods' rent (Article 640 of the Civil Act). Here, two periods do not necessarily mean two consecutive months. It is enough for the total overdue amount to reach two months' rent. Even if payments are missed one month at a time here and there, adding up to two months' rent, that can be grounds for termination.
Commercial premises: three periods

Commercial premises covered by the Commercial Building Lease Protection Act can be terminated only when the overdue amount reaches three periods' rent (Article 10-8 of that Act). A tenant who has ever been in arrears up to an amount equal to three periods' rent can be refused a request to renew the lease (Article 10(1)1 of that Act), and loses protection of the opportunity to recover key money (권리금) (proviso to Article 10-4(1) of that Act). This works differently from termination in that, once it has happened, it remains a ground for refusing renewal even if all the overdue amounts are paid later.
It ends only when notice of termination is received

Arrears alone do not end the contract automatically. It takes effect only when notice of termination is given and reaches the tenant. Since the time of termination must be proved in court, it is common to send it by certified mail (내용증명) setting out the arrears. If the tenant pays the overdue rent before notice and the overdue amount falls below the threshold, termination may no longer be possible, so make sure the date you calculated the arrears and the date of notice line up.

Some contracts include a special term allowing termination after even one missed payment, but an agreement that departs from Article 640 of the Civil Act to the tenant's disadvantage has no effect (Article 652 of the Civil Act). Rather than giving notice of termination based only on a special term, please first check whether the statutory requirements are met.
A judgment that settles the deposit at the same time

Even after the lease ends, if the landlord does not return the deposit, the tenant can refuse to vacate by asserting simultaneous performance. That is why, in eviction suits, landlords often seek a judgment ordering the tenant to hand over the building in exchange for payment of the deposit minus overdue rent, maintenance fees and an amount equivalent to rent until the premises are vacated.

Once the eviction judgment becomes final or is declared provisionally enforceable, you apply to a court enforcement officer for enforcement of delivery. You should also work out in advance the cost and schedule for dealing with belongings left on the day of enforcement, and if the tenant leaves their belongings and cuts off contact, opening the door or removing the belongings on your own can lead to criminal issues.

If possession passes to someone else during the lawsuit, enforcement may be blocked even after you win, so the proper order is to fix the occupant with a provisional injunction against transfer of possession (점유이전금지가처분) before filing. Also factor in that the longer the arrears continue, the less room there is to cover them with the deposit.

author: park-jongjin

title: Why a final payment order and a judgment do not have the same effect
summary: A final payment order can be enforced like a judgment, but it has no res judicata effect, leaving room for the debtor to dispute it again through an objection to the claim. This article separates cases suited to payment orders from those that are not.

body.text: Payment orders (지급명령) are widely used because they are fast and inexpensive. You often hear that if the debtor does not file an objection within 2 weeks of being served, it has the same effect as a final judgment (Articles 470 and 474 of the Civil Procedure Act). But there is something to note about the words ‘same effect’.
Same enforceability, different res judicata

A final payment order is no different from a judgment in that it can be used for seizure, collection and compulsory auction. In fact, in principle it can be enforced directly with the original of the payment order without obtaining a separate certificate of execution (Article 58(1) of the Civil Execution Act). But unlike a judgment, a final payment order is not given res judicata effect (기판력). Res judicata is the effect that prevents a final decision from being disputed again later.

So even after a payment order becomes final, the debtor can file a lawsuit objecting to the claim (청구이의의 소) based on grounds that existed before then, for example that the debt had already been paid before the payment order was issued or that there was never a debt in the first place. An objection to a judgment can only be based on grounds that arose after the hearings ended, but that restriction does not apply to payment orders (Article 58(3) of the Civil Execution Act).

For creditors, this difference may not often be a real problem. But if the other side belatedly files a lawsuit objecting to the claim together with an application to stay compulsory execution at the enforcement stage, recovery is delayed accordingly. If you see the seeds of a dispute in a case, factor this in from the outset.
Cases suited to a payment order

Payment orders are efficient for cases such as payment for goods or undisputed loans, where the amount is clear and the other side does not seem likely to contest it. The procedure is in writing and the stamp fee is one tenth of that for a complaint. If the other side does not object, you obtain an enforceable title without ever going to court.

On the other hand, in cases where the other side is sure to claim it was a gift or an investment, or where deductions will be disputed, an objection will turn it into a lawsuit in the end, and even if it becomes final, there remains room to dispute it again through an objection to the claim. For such cases, going to a lawsuit from the start may end up being faster.
When it cannot be used or gets blocked

A payment order can be applied for only if it can be served on the debtor by a method other than service by public notice (proviso to Article 462 of the Civil Procedure Act). If you don't know the other side's address, the right approach is to file a lawsuit from the start and find the address through a fact inquiry. If you apply with only a name and an old address, even if the order becomes final you may get stuck at the enforcement stage because the debtor cannot be identified, so it is a good idea to confirm the resident registration number or business registration number as well.

If you are the one who received a payment order, the 2-week period is what matters most. Simply filing an objection moves the matter to a lawsuit even without lengthy reasons, so if there is anything to dispute, you can file the objection within the period first and prepare your answer after that. The fast route is not always the short one. Please anticipate what the other side will dispute before choosing a procedure.

author: park-jongjin

title: Breach of contract or tort? The starting point for a damages claim
summary: Even for the same harm, what you must prove and the limitation period differ depending on whether you claim for non-performance of an obligation or for a tort. This article sets out the differences between the two paths and how to use them together.

body.text: The first question in a damages consultation is usually how much can be recovered. But before answering, there is something to decide first: whether the harm arose from a broken promise or from an unlawful act. Even for the same harm, what you must prove and the deadlines differ depending on which path you take.
What must be proved differs
