For liability for non-performance of an obligation (채무불이행), once you show the terms of the contract and the fact that it was not performed as agreed, the debtor can escape liability only by proving there was no intent or negligence on their part (Article 390 of the Civil Act). For liability in tort (불법행위), by contrast, the victim must prove all of the other party's intent or negligence, unlawfulness, the harm, and the causal link between them (Article 750 of the Civil Act).

Suppose a moving company damaged furniture while moving it. If framed as a breach of the transport contract, the company must show it was not at fault; if framed as a tort, the victim must show the company's negligence. This is why, in cases where there is a contractual relationship, non-performance is considered first.
Limitation periods differ

A claim for damages in tort expires 3 years from the date the victim learned of the harm and the wrongdoer, or 10 years from the date of the tort (Article 766 of the Civil Act). A contractual claim is 10 years for an ordinary civil claim and 5 years for a claim arising from a commercial activity. Even if a tort claim is barred after 3 years, there may still be a path if it can be framed as a breach of contract.

Here, the date you learned does not mean the date you first felt the harm, but the date you actually knew that harm had resulted from an unlawful act and who the wrongdoer was. If the calculation is unclear, it is better to go through materials date by date before concluding that it is too late.
Scope of compensation and consolation money

The scope of compensation for non-performance is in principle the damage that ordinarily arises, and damage arising from special circumstances is compensated only if the other party knew or could have known of those circumstances (Article 393 of the Civil Act). This provision also applies to torts (Article 763 of the Civil Act). Mental harm is recognized through consolation money (위자료) where body, liberty or reputation has been harmed (Article 751 of the Civil Act), but in cases involving only a breach of contract, once the financial loss is compensated, consolation money is often hard to obtain.
Comparative negligence also applies to both paths (Articles 396 and 763 of the Civil Act). Either way, if the victim was also at fault, the compensation may be reduced by that proportion.
If both are possible, use them together

If both claims can be made, argue them together in a single lawsuit so that if one is blocked, a decision can still be obtained on the other. Which one to put first depends on whether there is a written contract, what materials show the other party's fault, and how much time has passed. Organizing the date of the incident and whether there is a contract first will speed up the assessment.

If you are the one who received the complaint, look first at which path the other side chose. If the claim is in tort, point out where the plaintiff has failed to prove intent or negligence and causation, and also check whether the limitation period has expired.

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: Money and information to prepare before applying for provisional attachment
summary: Speed matters in provisional attachment, but if identifying the property or arranging security is delayed, the decision is delayed too. This article covers what information to have ready before applying and what to do within 2 weeks after the decision.

body.text: Many people come for an urgent consultation after hearing that the other party has put their home up for sale. Most agree that provisional attachment (가압류) is needed, but when it comes to actually proceeding, time is lost in two places: identifying the property to be frozen, and arranging the security the court orders. Both can be prepared before the consultation.
You can apply only once you decide what to freeze

Provisional attachment is not a procedure for vaguely freezing all of the other party's property; you apply by specifying particular property. For real estate, you check the owner in the certified copy of the register; for deposits, you need to know which banks the other party uses; and for wages, which company they work for. A provisional attachment of deposits in principle affects the balance at the time the decision is served on the bank, so even if you name several banks, nothing is frozen if there is no balance.

items: The other party's name and address, and date of birth if possible
The location of any real estate and a certified copy of the register
The names of banks where they are likely to have deposits
The name and address of their workplace
Money owed to the other party by others, and who owes it (business partners, landlords, etc.)

body.text: Freezing far more property than the amount claimed gives the other party grounds to object or claim damages. It is usual to set an order, for example targeting real estate if there is any, and otherwise deposits or wages.

If you know nothing about the other party's property, you may choose to obtain a judgment first and then find property through a property disclosure (재산명시) and property inquiry (재산조회). Property disclosure can only be used after an enforceable title such as a judgment has become final, so at the provisional attachment stage the court does not find property for you.
Arrange the security in advance

The court may order you to provide security against the damage the other party could suffer from the provisional attachment (Article 280 of the Civil Execution Act). Security is provided by depositing cash or securities, or by submitting a document showing a payment bond contract with a surety insurance company (Article 122 of the Civil Procedure Act). Depending on the property and the case, an order may require part of it in cash.

If you spend several days raising money after receiving the order to provide security, the property may be disposed of in the meantime. If you find out the approximate amount of security at the consultation stage and prepare the funds in advance, you can shorten the time it takes to reach a decision.
Two weeks after the decision, and the main action

A provisional attachment decision cannot be enforced once 2 weeks have passed from the date you were notified of it (Article 292(2) of the Civil Execution Act). For real estate, the court commissions the registration, and for deposits and wages, the decision takes effect only when it is served on the bank or company. Once enforcement is done, file the main lawsuit or a payment order promptly. If the other party applies for an order to file suit and you do not file within the period set by the court, the provisional attachment is cancelled (Article 287).

Even after the provisional attachment, you can still negotiate with the other party. Quite often, the mere fact that their property is frozen prompts the other party to get in touch first, and if an agreement is reached, the usual order is to release the provisional attachment after receiving the money owed.

The deposit or surety insurance you provided as security can be recovered through a procedure to cancel the security if you win the main action. Keep the deposit certificate and insurance policy safe until the case is over.

author: park-jongjin

title: The first week after your bank account or home is provisionally attached
summary: Provisional attachment comes without warning, so it is easy to panic the moment you find out. This article covers what the party subject to provisional attachment should check, the procedures available, and how to claim for losses after the attachment is lifted.

body.text: When withdrawals are blocked in your banking app, or you pull the property register and find a provisional attachment you knew nothing about, that day is usually the first you hear of it. This is because provisional attachment is often decided on the papers without calling in the other side. Rather than calling the creditor in a panic, the first step is to get hold of the decision.
First, check the decision

The decision states who provisionally attached which property, for how much and on what grounds. If it has not yet been served on you, check the file using the case number shown by the bank or on the register and get a copy. The decision also states a release amount (해방금액). By depositing this amount, you can ask for enforcement of the provisional attachment to be stopped or for enforcement already carried out to be cancelled (Articles 282 and 299 of the Civil Execution Act).

Provisional attachment only freezes property; it is not a procedure by which the creditor takes the money. For the creditor to actually be paid, they must win the main action and move on to a final seizure. That also means there are things you can do in the meantime.

If wages or deposits have been provisionally attached, the limits on seizure set by law also apply to provisional attachment. If even the portion needed for living expenses has been frozen, you can dispute that scope, so keep your bank transaction records and pay slips.
Choose how to challenge it

items: If there is no claim or the amount is excessive, an objection to the provisional attachment (Article 283)
If you have already paid or circumstances have changed, an application for cancellation due to changed circumstances (Article 288)
If the creditor does not file the main lawsuit, an application for an order to file suit (Article 287)
If you need to use the account right away, deposit of the release amount

body.text: There is no set deadline for an objection, but filing one does not automatically stop enforcement. If business funds are frozen and the matter is urgent, you can deposit the release amount to release them first and then challenge it through the objection procedure. If the creditor has only made the provisional attachment and keeps putting off the lawsuit, you can apply for an order to file suit so that they must file within a period set by the court.

When you file an objection, the court holds a hearing or an examination in which both sides take part (Article 286(1)). Bring contracts, transfer records and conversation records showing that there is no claim or that the amount has been inflated.
There is still work to do after it is lifted

If the provisional attachment was unjustified, you can claim for the losses it caused. The deposit or surety insurance the creditor provided as security exists precisely to cover such losses. If the creditor applies to cancel the security after the lawsuit ends, the court notifies the party subject to the provisional attachment to exercise their rights within a certain period, and if no damages suit or similar is filed within that period, they are deemed to have consented to cancelling the security (Article 125(3) of the Civil Procedure Act).

If you receive a notice from the court to exercise your rights, don't leave it; check the deadline first. Gathering materials in advance that show losses caused by the provisional attachment, such as lost business, blocked loans or costs spent on the objection procedure, will speed up the assessment. If the losses are not large, it is sometimes better to consent to cancelling the security and close the matter.
Avoid getting angry at the creditor or sending long messages explaining your circumstances because of the provisional attachment. Those messages can be used as evidence that you acknowledge the debt.

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: When a debtor who owes you money files for individual rehabilitation
summary: A creditor who receives a debtor's individual rehabilitation papers has tools such as a trial to examine and determine claims, an objection at the creditors' meeting and an application for an order to exercise avoidance rights. Each has a deadline, so this article goes through them in order.

body.text: Quite a few people who lent money to a business partner or acquaintance come to us for a consultation. They have received a commencement decision and a list of creditors from the court and don't know what to do. Creditors have more tools than you might think, but every one of them comes with a deadline.
If the amount is wrong, act within the objection period

A creditor who objects to the content of the list of individual rehabilitation creditors may apply in writing within the objection period for a trial to examine and determine individual rehabilitation claims (개인회생채권조사확정재판) (Article 604(1) of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act). The objection period is set at between 2 weeks and 2 months from the date of the commencement decision (Article 596(2)1). If you don't apply within this period, the claim is determined as stated in the list, and once entered in the creditor schedule, it has the same effect as a final judgment (Article 603).

If you were already suing the debtor, you don't apply separately; instead, that lawsuit is changed into a suit to examine and determine the claim (Article 604(2)). It is also easy to overlook that the application will be dismissed if you don't pay the costs in advance when applying (paragraph 4 of the same article).
Objections to the repayment plan are made at the meeting

At the creditors' meeting, creditors may state objections to the repayment plan (Article 613). If there is an objection, the court may approve the plan only if the amount repaid to the objecting creditor is at least what they would receive as a distribution in bankruptcy, the debtor puts all of their disposable income toward repayment, and the amount is at least the statutory minimum repayment (Article 614(2)). For an objection to carry weight, you need materials showing hidden income or assets, such as a shop the debtor runs, property moved into a spouse's name, or a vehicle disposed of just before the application.
If assets were siphoned off, an order to exercise avoidance rights

If the debtor transferred property knowing it would harm creditors, or repaid only certain creditors, you can apply to the court for an order requiring the debtor to exercise avoidance rights (부인권) (Article 584(3)). This cannot be exercised once 1 year has passed from the date of the commencement decision, so act quickly once you learn of the circumstances (paragraph 5 of the same article). If the other party has filed for bankruptcy, the bankruptcy trustee investigates the property, so hand your materials to the trustee; if you oppose a discharge, file an objection by showing grounds for refusing discharge within 30 days of the discharge examination date (Article 562).
No direct demands for payment; guarantors are separate

Once the commencement decision is made, compulsory execution or demands for repayment based on claims on the list are prohibited (Article 600(1)). Rather than contacting the debtor out of frustration to demand money, the right approach is to respond through the rehabilitation commissioner, and if after approval repayments do not come in and it is clear the plan cannot be carried out, you can apply for the proceedings to be discontinued (Article 621(1)). If there is a guarantor, you can claim against the guarantor regardless of the debtor's rehabilitation (Article 625(3)).

For corporate creditors, the day you receive a business partner's commencement decision is the day internal deadline management begins. The first task is to put the last day of the objection period and the meeting date stated in the decision on your calendar.

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: With four or fewer employees, can you dismiss as you please?
summary: The restrictions on unfair dismissal and the provisions on applications for remedy do not apply to workplaces with four or fewer regular employees. But if you don't know how employees are counted and which obligations still remain, you can get into trouble.

body.text: Article 11 of the Labor Standards Act applies to workplaces that regularly employ 5 or more workers. So in small shops and early-stage startups, people take it for granted that ‘we have fewer than 5 people, so dismissal is no problem.’ That is half right, because only certain provisions set by Presidential Decree apply to workplaces with 4 or fewer employees. The problem is the other half.
Provisions that drop out and provisions that remain

Workplaces with 4 or fewer employees are not subject to Article 23(1), which prohibits dismissal without just cause, Article 27, which requires the grounds and timing of dismissal to be given in writing, or Article 28, which provides for applications to the Labor Relations Commission for remedy against unfair dismissal (Appended Table 1 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act). So there will be no dispute before the Labor Relations Commission over whether the grounds for dismissal were justified.

That does not mean all obligations disappear. Advance notice of dismissal (Article 26), which requires notice 30 days in advance or payment of at least 30 days' ordinary wages, also applies to workplaces with 4 or fewer employees. Unless a statutory exception applies, such as for workers employed continuously for less than 3 months, you must pay the price for letting someone go without notice. Severance pay also applies to all businesses that employ workers (Article 3 of the Employee Retirement Benefit Security Act), so it must be handled separately for employees who have worked for 1 year or more.

Obligations set by other laws, such as the minimum wage, must also be observed regardless of workplace size. Being a workplace with 4 or fewer employees means that certain provisions of the Labor Standards Act do not apply; it does not mean you are exempt from labor laws as a whole.
How are the ‘four’ counted?

The part most often gotten wrong is counting employees. The number of regular employees is calculated by dividing the total number of workers employed during the 1 month before the date the legal issue, such as a dismissal, arose by the number of operating days in that period (Article 7-2 of the Enforcement Decree). It is not just full-time employees who count; fixed-term workers, part-time workers and casual part-timers are all included, regardless of the form of employment.

Even if the average is below 5, if the days with fewer than 5 workers are less than half of the total when counted day by day, the workplace is treated as having 5 or more. Conversely, even if the average is 5 or more, if the days with fewer than 5 are half or more, it is not treated that way. For a shop that uses several part-timers only on weekends, this calculation can change the conclusion.

items: Attendance records and payroll for the 1 month before the dismissal date
Working days of part-timers and part-time workers
Whether there are family employees and whether they work alongside other employees
Whether another shop run by the same owner is effectively one workplace

body.text: The smaller the company, the more you should keep documents

If the number of employees is near the threshold, the first dispute before the Labor Relations Commission will be over the number of regular employees. If you gave notice of dismissal only verbally thinking you had 4 or fewer, and it is found that you have 5 or more, the dismissal can lose its effect solely for failure to give written notice. Even if you are small, the habit of giving the grounds and timing of dismissal in writing, and getting a resignation letter in the case of a resignation, is what protects the company in the end.

When your headcount is growing, it is time to revise your employment rules and employment contracts together, because the number of provisions that apply increases all at once the moment you exceed 5 employees.

author: park-jongjin

title: Penalties for unpaid wages get heavier from October 8
summary: From October 8, 2026, the statutory penalty for failing to pay severance pay and wages rises to imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of up to 50 million won. This article sets out the changes employers should know, from the rule on non-desire for punishment to late-payment interest and treble damages.

body.text: The amended Labor Standards Act passed in April this year takes effect on October 8, 2026. Not many provisions change, but for companies that find it tight to meet payroll, the changes will weigh differently. That is because the statutory penalty for failing to pay what is owed to a departing employee on time is going up.
What changes

When an employee leaves, the employer must pay all money owed, including wages and severance pay, within 14 days, and if there are special circumstances, the date can be extended by agreement between the parties (Article 36). Until now, violating this obligation carried imprisonment for up to 3 years or a fine of up to 30 million won. For violations after October 8, when the amended Act takes effect, Article 107 applies and the penalty becomes heavier: imprisonment for up to 5 years or a fine of up to 50 million won.

Penal provisions in principle follow the law in force at the time of the act, so the previous statutory penalty applies to violations completed before the effective date. However, where non-payment continues past the effective date, which point in time is used as the standard must be examined case by case.

You should also know the procedure. When a former employee files a petition with the labor office, a labor inspector calls in both sides, confirms the amount unpaid and orders payment. If payment is not made by the deadline given, the matter may be turned into a criminal case and referred, and from that point the statutory penalty above becomes a real issue. It is usual to separate the amounts you accept from those you dispute and to pay the accepted portion first.
The rule on non-desire for punishment remains

Some articles say the amendment abolished the rule that a case cannot be prosecuted against the victim's wishes (반의사불벌), but the text shows otherwise. The provision that no indictment can be filed if the affected employee clearly states that they do not want punishment remains after the amendment. However, it does not apply where an employer whose name has been publicly disclosed for unpaid wages fails to pay wages again during the disclosure period.

In the end, a settlement with the employee remains the most realistic means of ending the criminal process in an unpaid wage case. With the statutory penalty going up, a settlement arguably matters even more.
Burdens that have grown beyond criminal punishment

items: Late-payment interest at 20 percent per year from the day after 14 days have passed since the employee left (Article 37, Article 17 of the Enforcement Decree)
Late-payment interest also where regular wages are not paid on the set date during employment (Article 37(1)2)

Where wages were withheld with clear intent, where wages went unpaid for a total of 3 months or more within 1 year, or where the total unpaid amount is 3 months' ordinary wages or more, the employee may ask the court for damages of up to 3 times the amount (Article 43-8)

body.text: Treble damages apply to grounds arising on or after October 23, 2025. The court sets the amount taking into account the period and circumstances of non-payment, how much effort the employer made to pay, late-payment interest already paid and the employer's financial situation. If non-payment is unavoidable, drawing up a payment plan and keeping a record of paying at least part of it first will matter in this assessment.

If cash flow makes it difficult to pay severance, start by signing an extension agreement with the employee before the 14 days are up. A single agreement stating the date and amount can make a big difference to late-payment interest and criminal liability.

author: park-jongjin

title: A response to an unfair dismissal remedy application starts from the dismissal notice
summary: When the Labor Relations Commission sends a copy of a remedy application, the company must prove that the dismissal was justified. This article sets out the order in which to prepare the response and the hearing.

body.text: A common trap companies fall into in Labor Relations Commission cases is thinking that because the employee did something wrong, the dismissal is naturally justified. When a dismissed employee applies for remedy, the company receives a copy of the application and a request to submit a response, and company heads usually have a lot to say: how long they put up with it, and how the other employees all knew. But the Labor Relations Commission looks at whether that story can be turned into a record.
Three things the company must prove

Whether the grounds for dismissal actually existed, whether those grounds were serious enough to justify dismissal, and whether the required procedures were followed. The company bears the burden of proving just cause for dismissal. The fact that you warned the employee verbally several times is hard to have recognized unless it is preserved in a warning letter or email.

A dismissal takes effect only if its grounds and timing are given in writing (Article 27 of the Labor Standards Act). The response should be written around the grounds stated in the notice. Bringing up new grounds in the response that were not in the notice weakens its persuasiveness, and if the grounds in the notice are too abstract, that itself may be pointed out as a procedural problem.
What to do in the week you receive the copy

items: Put the deadline for the response set by the Labor Relations Commission on the calendar
Check the original dismissal notice and how it was sent (mail, email, messenger)
Gather the notice of the disciplinary committee, its minutes and records of giving the employee a chance to explain
Break down the employee's claims item by item and mark which ones you have rebuttal materials for and which you don't

body.text: Doing this marking exercise reveals the company's weak points. If the grounds are clear but you skipped the notice convening the disciplinary committee required by the employment rules, the dismissal may be found unfair even if the grounds are sufficient. You need to know your weak points first to decide whether to settle or fight to the end.

In the response, set out in order the background of the case, the facts and evidence for each ground of dismissal, why the disciplinary measure was proportionate, and how the procedures were followed. If you rebut the parts of the employee's claims that are untrue using matching item numbers, it is easier for the commissioners to read both sides' arguments side by side.

If there are 4 or fewer regular employees, the provisions restricting dismissal and on remedy applications do not apply. However, the number of regular employees is calculated by dividing the total number of workers over a set period by the number of operating days, so recount including part-timers.
The hearing and settlement

After the investigator's fact-finding, a hearing is held at which the commissioners question both sides directly. It is a good idea to practice in advance with expected questions so that the answers of the company head or HR manager do not contradict the response. If you number the evidence submitted with the response and indicate in the text which argument each item supports, you can find and point to it immediately at the hearing too.

The Labor Relations Commission may recommend a settlement before issuing its decision, and a settlement reached has the same effect as a judicial settlement (Article 16-3 of the Labor Relations Commission Act). If there are flaws in the procedure, it is worth comparing a monetary settlement rather than waiting for the decision. This is because if a remedy order is not complied with after a finding of unfair dismissal, a non-compliance penalty of up to 30 million won can be imposed repeatedly, up to twice a year (Article 33 of the Labor Standards Act).

If you disagree with the decision, you can apply to the National Labor Relations Commission for review within 10 days of being notified of the written decision (Article 31). The deadline is short, so be sure to note the date you received the decision.

author: kang-hyunwoo

title: Penalty clauses: look at their nature before the numbers
summary: A penalty in a contract may be liquidated damages, which a court can reduce, or a contractual penalty, which it may not. This article explains why you should settle which one it is in the wording before signing.

body.text: The first thing companies ask when they bring us a contract to review is usually the amount: isn't a penalty of twice the contract price too much, or conversely, isn't the penalty we would receive too small? But there is something to look at before the amount: what legal nature that money has.
A penalty is presumed to be liquidated damages

Article 398(4) of the Civil Act presumes that an agreement on a penalty is a predetermination of damages (손해배상액의 예정), i.e. liquidated damages. Liquidated damages are a device that allows you to claim the agreed amount when a dispute arises without proving how much the actual loss was. This is convenient for the receiving side, but it comes with a limitation: even if the actual loss exceeds the predetermined amount, it is in principle hard to receive more than that.

If the predetermined amount is unreasonably high, the court may reduce it appropriately (paragraph 2 of the same article). So for the paying side, the amount written in the contract is not the end of the story. There remains room to seek a reduction based on the size of the transaction, how the breach happened and the loss that could actually arise.

Having liquidated damages also does not take away the right to demand performance or to rescind the contract (paragraph 3 of the same article). You can choose separately whether to end the deal while receiving the penalty or to keep demanding performance. Delay penalties (지체상금) charged per day when delivery or construction runs late raise the same issue. Without a cap, they can exceed the contract price as the delay drags on, and then too, whether to reduce them becomes an issue.
What changes if you write ‘contractual penalty’

If the contract clearly states that the penalty is a contractual penalty (위약벌), things may be different. A contractual penalty is money received as a sanction for breach, so it is generally considered claimable separately from damages, and the reduction provision in Article 398(2) may not apply as is. However, an excessively heavy contractual penalty may be partly void as contrary to public order.

Even with the same figure, the size of the company's liability differs depending on whether it is liquidated damages or a contractual penalty, and whether actual losses can be claimed separately. If this is left blank, any dispute will start with an argument over interpretation.
Is your company the receiving side or the paying side?

If you are more likely to receive the penalty, consider adding a sentence that actual losses can be claimed separately from the penalty, or stating that it is a contractual penalty. If you are more likely to pay, specify that the penalty is liquidated damages and include an overall liability cap and an exclusion of indirect damages.

When reviewing, check in turn whether the nature of the penalty is settled in the wording, whether actual losses can be claimed separately from the penalty, whether there is an overall liability cap and an exclusion of indirect damages, and whether a cure period is given to correct a breach.
Even if the other side has used the form dozens of times, these few lines are worth negotiating. Once you have signed, there is not much you can do other than hope for a reduction by the court.

author: park-jongjin

title: Asking a business partner to revise a contract: there is an order to it
summary: Many people worry that asking for revisions will break the deal. This article explains how to sort out what to fix first rather than holding on to every clause.

body.text: “If we ask for this many changes, won't the other company be unhappy?” That is what clients add most often when they bring us a contract to review. The side that receives the other party's form always feels like the weaker party. But when deals actually fall through, the problem was often not the request for revisions itself but the way it was made.
Sort clauses into three columns

When you receive a contract, sort the clauses into those you must fix, those worth negotiating and those you can accept. Clauses with no cap on damages or that require compensation for ‘all losses’, clauses that let only the other side terminate, and clauses with vague payment timing usually go in the first column. Clauses such as the competent court or the method of notice often go in the second.

The trick is to narrow the first column down to no more than two or three. If you send back a contract with red lines in twenty places, the other side's contact person will pass it straight to their legal team, and from then on the schedule gets longer.

If it is a form the other side uses unchanged with many business partners, it may be regarded as standard terms and conditions. The Act on the Regulation of Terms and Conditions treats contract terms prepared in advance for contracting with multiple parties as standard terms regardless of their name or form (Article 2 of that Act), and makes unfair clauses void. Some companies carefully add this point as grounds for their revision request.
Send the revised wording together with the reason

If you only send “This clause is a problem,” the other side won't know what to accept. Instead, write the replacement sentence yourself and add a line or two on why it is needed, and you will get a faster reply. For example, if you propose capping damages at the contract price while excepting intent or gross negligence, the other side also has a reason to accept it.

Look at penalties in terms of numbers. A penalty is presumed to be liquidated damages and can be reduced by the court if excessive (Article 398 of the Civil Act), but things may be different if the contract describes it as a contractual penalty (위약벌). The direction of the revision is also reversed depending on whether your company is the paying side or the receiving side.

Reading only the main text and skipping the attachments is another common mistake. If a specification or quotation says something different from the main text, you need to settle which one prevails, and also check whether delivery dates or unit prices agreed verbally in meetings made it into the final version.
If some clauses could not be changed in the end

Some clauses cannot be changed even through negotiation. In that case, set out by email how you understand the clause as you sign, and send it to the other side once. Record in the same way anything the other side's contact person said verbally, such as “we don't actually use that clause.”
If a dispute arises later, records like these are what gets looked at after the contract. A few emails exchanged in the days before signing can protect the company's position years later.

Finally, check the authority of the person signing. If someone other than the CEO is signing for the other side, check whether that person has authority to contract on the company's behalf, and whether the deal requires board approval within your own company.

title: The limitation period for payment for goods may be 3 years, not 5
summary: Companies that remember only the 5-year limitation period for commercial claims sometimes miss a short 3-year period. This article looks at limitation periods by type of receivable and how to stop the clock.

body.text: When talking about a company's receivables, you often hear that ‘commercial claims last 5 years.’ That is not wrong. Article 64 of the Commercial Act sets the extinctive prescription period for claims arising from commercial activities at 5 years. The problem is the proviso in the same article: if another law provides a shorter period, that provision applies.
The 3-year periods in the Civil Act

Article 163 of the Civil Act lists claims that expire after 3 years. Even picking out only the items relevant to company practice, there are quite a few: payment for products and goods sold by producers and merchants, claims relating to the work of craftsmen and manufacturers, claims of a contractor relating to construction work, and fees and interest set for periods of 1 year or less.

So a manufacturer's payment for delivered goods or a wholesaler's or retailer's payment for goods sold on credit may need to be acted on within 3 years. Equipment rental fees payable monthly may also be subject to the short period. Which category applies has to be determined by looking at the transaction, so lumping everything together as a single line of ‘receivables’ in your books is risky.

items: Payment for goods sold by a merchant and claims relating to a manufacturer's work: 3 years
A contractor's claim for construction payments: also 3 years
Other claims from commercial activities: 5 years in principle
Claims confirmed by a judgment or mediation: 10 years (Article 165 of the Civil Act)

body.text: The limitation period runs from when payment can be claimed. If a payment date was set, it runs from that date; if not, in principle from the time of delivery. For transactions with deliveries in several installments, the period can run separately for each one, so if you relax by looking only at the date of the last transaction, the oldest payments may expire first.
A certified letter alone does not stop the clock

The limitation period is interrupted by a claim, by seizure, provisional attachment or provisional injunction, or by the debtor's acknowledgment (Article 168 of the Civil Act). What is often misunderstood here is the certified letter (내용증명). Demanding payment by certified letter is only an out-of-court demand (최고), and such a demand does not interrupt the limitation period unless you take a step such as a lawsuit or provisional attachment within 6 months (Article 174 of the Civil Act).

If the limitation period has only a few months left, think of the 6 months from the date you send the certified letter not as a deadline but as a starting point. Conversely, if the business partner stamped a balance confirmation or acknowledged the remaining debt while paying part of it, the period may start running anew because of that acknowledgment, so keep such documents together separately.

The longer you have dealt with a partner, the more you tend to put off demanding payment. If you establish a practice of exchanging receivable balance confirmations every quarter, you can manage limitation periods without harming the relationship. If you have claims that are already close to 3 years old, we recommend considering a payment order or provisional attachment first, even if the amounts are not large.

Provisional attachment both stops the limitation period and freezes the other party's property. If you hear rumors that a business partner's situation is deteriorating, that is one more reason to move quickly, regardless of the limitation period.
